title: Schema ledger smokeplaybook: adaptive JSON-mode conformance & constrained-decoding tests
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a lightweight, reproducible smokeplaybook and test harness (the 'schema ledger') that exercises end-to-end JSON mode enforcement and constrained decoding across streaming responses and interleaved tool/function calls. The goal is to detect regressions where partial streams, toolcall boundaries, or model rollouts cause schema drift or silent degradations. This ticket scopes the test definitions, minimal orchestrator shim, and a set of deterministic fuzz+golden cases for CI canary runs.
acceptance_criteria: A schema ledger repository containing 20+ canonical scenarios (stream partials, tool interleaving, truncated KV cache) exists in CI and runs in <30s for a smoke run
Constrained-decoding validator returns deterministic verdicts (pass/warn/fail) and records first-failure token offsets
Failures produce human-readable remediation hints (e.g., increase max_tokens, use schema-relaxation, pin model variant)
Playbook includes at least 3 canary deployments that gate runtime-1.20 merges using the smoke tests
Observed false-positive rate <= 5% across baseline models (gpt-style-open-variants) during initial 1-week A/B
implementation_plan: Design: define 'ledger entry' format (schema-id, prompt template, expected schema, strictness profile, model-variants)
Harness: implement lightweight runner that streams to test model instances and records partial-emits and toolcall boundaries
Validator: constrained-decoder wrapper that replays tokens and reports conformance with token-level diagnostics
Integration: CI job that runs smokeplaybook on PRs touching runtime, jsonmode, and tool-call routing
Canary: wire three runtime canaries (hosted-staging, dedicated-staging, private-smoke) to fail PRs on critical regressions
test_cases: Partial-streamed-object: JSON object emitted across multiple stream frames with an intentional boundary inside a string (expect: pass after reassembly)
Interrupted-toolcall: model emits tool call, then extra tokens that violate the expected tool-return schema (expect: fail and classify as tool-call interference)
KV-cache-staleness: produce previously cached prefix then change schema mid-stream (expect: warn and record schema-diff)
Truncated-final-token: last token cut, leaving trailing comma; validator should attempt graceful repair and mark non-fatal if repair heuristic succeeds
Backoff-retry-compat: constrained-decoder invoked after model fallback to quantized variant; ensure that schema adherence metrics are comparable within tolerance
progress_updates: 2025-01-12: Spike complete — prototyped ledger entry format and a minimal runner that replays recorded token streams. Notes: streaming chunks may split UTF-8 graphemes; use byte-aware reassembly.
2025-01-22: PoC validator implemented that flags token-offset of first schema violation. Observed 12% false positives on noisy regression set (next: add repair heuristics and soft-warn level).

2025-02-02: Design review with PM and DX (Ruth, Omar). Decision: validator will export severity levels (pass/warn/fail) and suggested remediation strings for operator UI in Console. Documented in design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/structured-output/schema-ledger
2025-02-10: Integrated two canaries — hosted-staging and dedicated-staging — with CI smoke job. Private-smoke requires infra onboarding; blocked on ENG-20500 network credential rotations.
2025-02-18: Reduced false positives to 4.3% after adding schema-relaxation profiles and whitespace-tolerant tokenizer. Moving to broaden model set for baseline run.
notes: Trade-offs considered: strict failure vs. warn semantics. We prioritize availability; default smoke job will warn on non-critical relaxations but fail on toolcall schema mismatches.
Edge-case: streaming tool calls that interleave 'content' tokens and 'tool' tokens require canonicalization before validation — we'll normalize to a unified token stream with boundary markers.
Operational: record minimal diagnostics (schema-id, model-variant, token-offset, first-failure-snippet, run-id) to keep telemetry <1KB per failure.
Future: consider a regression dashboard that aggregates ledger diffs across releases and surfaces flaky prompts for eval teams.
risks: High false-positive spike on aggressive quantized backfills could create noise and block merges — mitigated by per-model tolerance profiles
Private-smoke runway dependent on infra credential rotation ticket (ENG-20500)
Validator performance overhead may add latency to canary runs; smoke job designed to be fast (<30s) by limiting token length and using cached model endpoints
implementation_notes: Validator will be implemented as a sidecar library in runtime validation package (go + rust FFI shim). Start with JS/TS harness for rapid iteration in CI.
Use stable canonicalizer that preserves toolcall boundaries: markers <<TOOL_START:toolName>> and <<TOOL_END>> before validation.
Store ledger entries as plain JSONL with small fixtures; keep human-editable templates in /playbooks/ledger/
next_steps: Finalize schema-id naming convention and publish to Confluence
Merge GH proto runner PR and enable smoke job on runtime-1.20 branch
Coordinate with infra to unblock private-smoke (ENG-20500)
Schedule a 1-hour demo with QA, DX, and PM to review initial smoke results (week of 2025-02-24)
